Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called "al-Mulk" (The Sovereignty) because it opens with the glorification of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in whose hand is the sovereignty, and who is over all things capable. It also mentions matters that belong only to one who possesses complete sovereignty and absolute disposal, and that is Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Among the Aims of the Surah

• Mention of a group of Allah's attributes of greatness, such as His sole possession of sovereignty and complete power; His creation of the heavens in a manner of utmost perfection and their adornment with shining stars; a reminder of the favour of creating the earthly world and the precision of its order and its suitability for human life. All of this is evidence of the oneness of Allah in His divinity.

• A warning to people against the plotting of the devils; a clarification that salvation lies in following the Messenger (ﷺ) and loss lies in denying him; an alert to the obstinate to the encompassing knowledge of Allah over all created beings; and a comparison between the fate of the disbelievers and the believers, in the manner of the Qur'an combining warning with glad tidings.

• A dispelling of hope among the polytheists in relying on idols for their support or for their provision; a rebuke for their disbelief in the blessing of Allah and their hastening of the death of the Prophet (ﷺ); and a warning to them of the punishments of this world and the torment of the Hereafter that will befall them.

[The Tafsir]

Abundant is the goodness and kindness of Allah toward all His creation, in whose hand is the sovereignty of this world and the Hereafter and their authority; His command and decree prevail over both, and He is over all things capable. It is derived from the verse that the attribute of "hand" is affirmed for Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in a manner befitting His majesty.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 2:**

He is the One who created death and life, to test you, O people: which of you is best in deed and most sincere in it? He is the Mighty, whom nothing can overpower, the Forgiving toward whoever of His servants repents. In the verse there is encouragement to perform acts of obedience and a warning against committing sins.

Surely, He is the One who created seven heavens, layered one above another, in harmony. You, O observer, will see no inconsistency or disparity in the creation of the Most Merciful. So look again at the sky: do you see any cracks or fissures in it?
Then repeat your gaze again and again; your sight will return to you humbled and degraded, unable to find any flaw, while it is exhausted and weary.

And We adorned the nearest heaven, the one that the eyes see, with great, shining stars. We made them missiles that burn the devils who eavesdrop on the angels. And for them in the Hereafter We have prepared the punishment of the blazing Fire, in which they will suffer its heat.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 67, verse 6:**

For those who disbelieve in their Creator is the punishment of Hell, and evil is their final destination: Hell.
When these disbelievers are thrown into Hell, they will hear from it a terrible, dreadful roaring sound, while it boils with a fierce boiling.

Hell will almost burst apart with rage against the disbelievers. Whenever a group of people is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them with reproach: "Did no warner come to you in the worldly life to warn you of this punishment you are in?"

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Simplified Commentary") on Surah 67, verse 9:

They will answer them, saying: "Yes, indeed a messenger came to us from Allah and warned us, but we denied him. We said about what he brought of the signs: 'Allah has not sent down anything upon any human being. You, O messengers, are only in a far-reaching error from the truth.'"

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 10:

And they will say, acknowledging their guilt: "If we had listened with the listening of one who seeks the truth, or had reflected upon that to which we were called, we would not have been among the companions of the Fire."
They will confess their denial and their disbelief, which made them deserving of the punishment of the Fire. So, far removed from the mercy of Allah are the people of the Fire.

Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen, [who] worship Him and do not disobey Him while they are absent from people's eyes, and who dread the punishment of the Hereafter before witnessing it, will have forgiveness from Allah for their sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 13:

"And keep your speech secret, or make it public, [O people], regarding any of your affairs; both are the same to Allah. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of what is concealed within the breasts. So how could your words and deeds be hidden from Him?"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 14:

Does not the Lord of the worlds know His creation and their affairs? He is the One who created them and perfected their creation and made it excellent. He is the Subtle (al-Latif) toward His servants, the All-Aware of them and of their deeds.

Allah alone is the One who made the earth easy and smooth for you, a place where you settle, so walk through its regions and its sides, and eat of the provision of Allah which He brings forth for you from it, and to Him alone is the resurrection from your graves for reckoning and recompense. In the verse there is an exhortation to seek provision and gains, and in it is an indication that Allah is the true God, alone, with no partner, and of His power, and a reminder of His blessings, and a warning against inclining toward this world.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verses 16–17:

Have you become secure, O disbelievers of Makkah, from Him who is above the heaven, that He might cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes with you until you are destroyed? Or have you become secure from Him who is above the heaven, that He might send upon you a storm of pebbles, so that you will know, O disbelievers, how My warning to you was, when you witness the punishment? And knowledge will not benefit you at that time. And in the verse is the affirmation of Allah's elevation (ʿuluw), as befits His majesty, glory be to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verses 16–17:

Have you become secure, O disbelievers of Makkah, from Him who is above the heaven, that He might cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes with you until you are destroyed? Or have you become secure from Him who is above the heaven, that He might send upon you a storm of pebbles, so that you will know, O disbelievers, how My warning to you was, when you witness the punishment? And knowledge will not benefit you at that time. And in the verse is the affirmation of Allah's elevation (ʿuluw), as befits His majesty, glory be to Him.

And indeed, those who came before them, the disbelievers of Makkah, denied their messengers, like the people of Nuh, 'Ad and Thamud. So how was My rejection of them, and My changing of the blessing they had into punishment by sending down the torment upon them and destroying them?

Have these disbelievers been heedless and not looked at the birds above them, spreading their wings in their flight through the air, and sometimes folding them in to their sides? Nothing holds them up from falling at such times except the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). Indeed, He is All-Seeing of everything; no flaw or disparity can be seen in His creation. Rather, who is this [that] you believe, O disbelievers, to be a host (ḥizb) for you, who would help you apart from the Most Merciful, if He wished harm for you? The disbelievers, in this their assumption, are only in delusion and misguidance from Satan. Rather, who is this supposed provider who would provide for you if God withheld His provision and denied it to you? Rather, the disbelievers persisted in their transgression and misguidance, in obstinacy, arrogance, and aversion from the truth, not listening to it and not following it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 67, verse 22:

Is he who walks stooped, face-down, not knowing where he is going or how he is heading, more upright on the path and better guided? Or he who walks upright, standing tall, safe, on a clear path with no crookedness in it? This is a parable that God has struck for the disbeliever and the believer.

Say to them, O Messenger: "It is Allah who brought you into being from nothing, and made for you hearing, by which you hear, and sight, by which you see, and hearts, by which you understand. Little are you grateful, O disbelievers, for these blessings to your Lord who bestowed them upon you." Say to them: "It is Allah who created you and scattered you across the earth, and to Him alone you will be gathered after this dispersal, for reckoning and recompense."

Little are you grateful, O disbelievers, for these blessings to your Lord who bestowed them upon you." Say to them: "It is Allah who created you and scattered you across the earth, and to Him alone you will be gathered after this dispersal, for reckoning and recompense."

The disbelievers say: "When will this promise of the Gathering be fulfilled, O Muhammad? Tell us its time, O believers, if you are truthful in what you claim."

Say, O Messenger, to these people: "Knowledge of the time of the Hour is exclusive to Allah, and I am only a warner to you, warning you of the consequence of your disbelief, and making clear to you, in the fullest clarity, what Allah has commanded me to make clear."

When the disbelievers see God's punishment near them, witnessing it with their own eyes, humiliation and dejection will appear on their faces, and it will be said to them as a rebuke: "This is what you used to demand be hastened in the world."

Say, [O Messenger], to these disbelievers: Tell me, if Allah causes me and those believers with me to die, as you wish, or has mercy on us and delays our terms, and spares us from His punishment, then who will protect you and shield you from a painful, agonizing punishment?

Say: "He is the Most Merciful. We have believed in Him, acted upon His law, obeyed Him, and placed our trust in Him alone in all our affairs. So you will know, O disbelievers, when the punishment descends: which of the two groups, ours or yours, is in clear error, far from the straight path of God?"

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: Tell me, if your water that you drink were to sink away into the earth, so that you could not reach it by any means, who other than Allah could bring you flowing water upon the surface of the earth, visible to the eyes?
